question: Will Russia, India, and China hold a trilateral (three-way) meeting before September 1, 2026?
background:
The Russia-India-China (“RIC troika”) format has been an intermittent forum for trilateral dialogue [since the early 2000s](https://valdaiclub.com/a/highlights/russia_india_china_trilateral_cooperation_and_prospects/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and is geopolitically salient because coordinated statements or cooperation among these three major Eurasian powers could shift global diplomatic and economic alignments. Russia has [recently pushed](https://thediplomat.com/2025/07/is-the-russia-india-china-troika-making-a-comeback/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) for a revival of RIC diplomacy, but China and India’s willingness to participate at the leaders’ level is uncertain because of India–China border disputes and strategic frictions and India’s multi-alignment policy. Media coverage around recent [Shanghai Cooperation Organization](https://www.chathamhouse.org/2025/09/modis-sco-summit-visit-shows-china-and-india-want-reset-relations-dragon-elephant-tango?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and other summits has repeatedly flagged discussion of RIC revivals and occasional three-way huddles on the margins of larger meetings. 

Tracking whether the three heads of state/government actually hold a dedicated trilateral leaders’ meeting by the end of August 2026 is therefore a crisp signal of changing geopolitical dynamics.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if, before September 1, 2026, there is a scheduled trilateral meeting (in-person or virtual) in which either (a) the heads of state/government of Russia, India, and China or (b) their foreign ministers simultaneously participate in the joint discussion. The meeting must be explicitly described as a trilateral/RIC (Russia-India-China) leaders’ meeting in an official communique, or foreign ministry statement (for [example](https://www.mea.gov.in/outoging-visit-detail.htm?30670/RussiaIndiaChina+Trilateral)) or by at least **two** reputable independent news agencies (e.g., Reuters, The Diplomat, Associated Press, BBC) quoting official sources.

question: Will the People's Republic of China blockade or quarantine Taiwan before September 1, 2026?
background:
CSIS: [How China Could Quarantine Taiwan: Mapping Out Two Possible Scenarios](https://www.csis.org/analysis/how-china-could-quarantine-taiwan-mapping-out-two-possible-scenarios)

> China has significantly increased pressure on Taiwan in recent years. China’s military [frequently flies aircraft](https://chinapower.csis.org/analysis/2022-adiz-violations-china-dials-up-pressure-on-taiwan/) within the island’s air defense identification zone (ADIZ) and across the Taiwan Strait median line. In August 2022 and April 2023, China escalated in response to U.S.-Taiwan political engagements by staging unprecedented large-scale [military exercises](https://chinapower.csis.org/analyzing-chinas-response-to-taiwan-president-tsai-ing-wen-transit/) around Taiwan. China has also [deployed](https://www.cga.gov.tw/GipOpen/wSite/ct?xItem=160424\&ctNode=8195\&mp=9996) its navy and coast guard in increasing numbers around Taiwan and its outlying islands.

> Cross-Strait tensions further intensified in the wake of William Lai’s inauguration as Taiwan’s president on May 20, 2024. Three days after Lai delivered his [inauguration address](https://english.president.gov.tw/News/6726), China commenced two days of large-scale military exercises surrounding Taiwan, called “[Joint Sword-2024A,](https://english.news.cn/20240523/2e8ebbb3171a4f4e96e0147f35fd1df4/c.html)” and accompanied them with “[comprehensive law enforcement operations](https://ccg.gov.cn/lbt/202405/t20240523_2253.html)” (综合执法演练) involving China’s coast guard. Chinese officials [stated](http://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html) that the drills were intended to “serve as a strong punishment for the separatist acts of ‘Taiwan independence’ forces and a stern warning against the interference and provocation by external forces.”
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as **Yes** if, before September 1, 2026, the U.S. executive branch publicly accuses the People's Republic of China of [blockading](https://www.britannica.com/topic/blockade-warfare), quarantining, closing or otherwise intentionally restricting maritime traffic entering at least one of Taiwan's seaports.

Please note that military exercises, simulated blockades, or other actions that have the effect of restricting maritime traffic to Taiwan do not count without an accusation as detailed above.

question: Will Italy's Schengen suspension against Spain be lifted before August 30, 2026?
background:
On [July 31, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Morocco%E2%80%93Spain_border_incident), roughly [50-60,000 migrants](https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-01/ultima-hora-de-la-entrada-de-inmigrantes-a-ceuta-en-directo.html) crossed by sea from Morocco into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta. The incident followed a Spanish Supreme Court ruling regarding returns of migrants who arrive by sea, with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez [stating that](https://apnews.com/article/spain-ceuta-migration-66839d113f24ba80d08b36d2b337201c) migrant smugglers had misinterpreted the ruling and deceived people.

In response to the situation, several European countries [offered support](https://www.democrata.es/en/international/macron-shows-his-support-for-sanchez-over-the-ceuta-crisis-and-proposes-backing-spain-through-frontex/) to Spain, while [others called](https://www.politico.eu/article/ceuta-crisis-migration-france-spain-border-checks-schengen-unity-morocco/) for Spain to be suspended from Schengen. By the following day, the majority of migrants had [returned to Morocco](https://apnews.com/article/spain-ceuta-migration-66839d113f24ba80d08b36d2b337201c), with the Spanish Interior Ministry estimating that roughly 48,300 had returned by Friday evening; while at least 67 people have died.

During the crisis, Italy [announced](https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/07/31/italy-suspends-schengen-with-spain-over-ceuta-migrant-crisis-shuts-air-and-sea-borders) it was temporarily suspending the Schengen Agreement with Spain, stating that the move was necessary to safeguard national security, and also criticising Spanish immigration policy. Spain subsequently summoned Italy's ambassador, and opponents of the Italian government [decried it](https://www.reuters.com/world/italy-suspends-eu-schengen-free-travel-pact-with-spain-over-ceuta-crisis-2026-07-31/) as a purely political move, due to Ceuta's [special rules](https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/07/31/migrants-in-ceuta-cannot-move-to-other-countries-eu-says) governing free movement.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if Italy's Schengen suspension against Spain stops being in effect at any time after this question opens and before August 30, 2026.

question: Will the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool be fully repaired before September 2026?
background:
The [Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Memorial_Reflecting_Pool) is a large, shallow rectangular pool on the National Mall, in Washington, D.C., located between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument.

In recent years, the pool has been plagued with algae. In April 2026, President Donald Trump announced that the pool would receive a new coating, in "American flag blue," using the ["latest and greatest filament."](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-resurfacing-lincoln-memorial-reflecting-pool-blue/) Trump also estimated that the repair would take a week and cost about \$1.5 million.

On May 11, 2026, as work on the pool continued, [a lawsuit was filed](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.292242/gov.uscourts.dcd.292242.1.0.pdf) to halt the work, and it was revealed that the cost of the repairs had ballooned, to [\$13.1 million](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/11/us/politics/reflecting-pool-paint-contract-trump.html), set to be paid to a contractor that Trump had selected. Over \$1M more was paid to another contractor, for algae treatment.

The repairs were deemed completed on June 5, 2026, but within a week [algae was again observed](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/12/algae-resurfaces-in-reflecting-pool-multi-million-dollar-renovation-00960609) in the pool, which the administration declared was ["residual."](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/10/politics/algae-reflecting-pool-trump) Within another week, observers noticed that the pool's new coat of paint was [already peeling](https://wtop.com/dc/2026/06/blue-paint-on-bottom-of-reflecting-pool-appears-to-be-peeling-away/), which the administration blamed on vandalism. [Several people](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/6-people-arrested-connection-alleged-vandalism-reflecting-pool-trump-s-rcna351409) have been arrested for allegedly damaging the pool, though some reporting has [cast doubt](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/us/trump-reflecting-pool-green-peeling.html) on the government's assertions.

On June 21, 2026, Trump announced that repairs to the pool would immediately [begin again](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/116790016615762850), and one contractor estimated that the work would take a matter of [weeks](https://www.eenews.net/articles/reflecting-pool-repairs-will-take-weeks-contractor-says/). In the meantime, the lawsuit to halt work on the pool remains pending.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, on September 1, 2026, the repairs to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool have been completed for at least one week and no credible sources are reporting that the pool is scheduled for or in need of further repairs.

question: Will the Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF drop at least $0.25 within two days before September 2026?
background:
Catastrophe bonds are insurance-linked securities that let insurers and reinsurers transfer the risk of natural disasters to capital-market investors. In calm periods investors collect an attractive yield; on the other hand, they can lose principal if a covered event (generally a hurricane, flood, earthquake, or wildfire) breaches the bond's predefined trigger.

The [Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF](https://ilsetf.com/ils) (NYSEARCA: ILS), launched in April 2025 as the first US-listed catastrophe bond ETF, holds a diversified portfolio of [roughly 102 such bonds](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4910536-ils-year-of-existence-revisiting-this-catastrophe-bond-fund-downgrade), heavily weighted toward US exposure. ILS is actively managed and its holdings may change at the discretion of its managers. ILS has little sensitivity to interest-rate fluctuations as its yield is floating-rate.

ILS trades near \$20 and has been remarkably stable, with its entire 52-week range spanning under a dollar. A drop of \$0.25 (about 1.25%) would therefore be an outsized move for this fund, most plausibly driven by a major catastrophe forcing markdowns across exposed holdings or by a broad repricing of catastrophe bond risk. A decline of that size would imply a disaster severe enough to threaten billions in insured losses, on the scale that has historically dented the entire catastrophe bond market.

The window of this question coincides with peak danger months: the Atlantic hurricane season began June 1 and runs into November, while Western US wildfire activity typically intensifies through summer and early fall.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, on any trading day after June 15, 2026 and before September 1, 2026, the Adjusted Close price of the Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF (NYSEARCA: ILS), as reported by [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ILS/), is at least \$0.25 lower than its Adjusted Close on the most recent trading day at least two calendar days earlier.

question: Will any U.S. state or EU member state restrict large-scale data center grid connections before September 2026?
background:
The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure has placed unprecedented pressure on electricity grids across the United States and Europe. The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) [projected in January 2026](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/Jan26.pdf) that electricity demand growth will accelerate significantly, with large computing facilities identified as a primary driver. The U.S. Department of Energy has [similarly identified data centers](https://www.energy.gov/oe/clean-energy-resources-meet-data-center-electricity-demand) as a critical short-term demand factor.

In Europe, grid connection queues [have reached record lengths](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/04/denmark-data-centers-moratorium-grid-pause-power-demand.html) in Ireland, the Netherlands, and Denmark — jurisdictions that have previously imposed informal or formal restrictions on new data center connections. Ireland's EirGrid and the Dutch transmission operator TenneT have both taken administrative action to limit new connections in recent years, establishing a precedent base rate for this type of regulatory action.

As of May 2026, several U.S. states including Virginia, Texas, and Georgia — home to the [largest data center concentrations](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/04/13/most-new-data-centers-in-the-us-are-coming-to-rural-areas/) in the country — are actively reviewing grid capacity allocation for high-load facilities.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, at any point before September 1, 2026, either a U.S. state or an EU member state announces a new moratorium, suspension, or binding restrictive rule applying to new grid connection requests from large-scale data centers, and the restriction is not officially reversed or rescinded before September 1, 2026, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

Large-scale datacenters are defined as facilities with contracted or requested grid capacity of 50 MW or more.

question: Will a new cultivated meat product receive regulatory approval for commercial sale before July 2027?
background:
Cultivated meat, also known as cultured meat, is genuine animal meat produced by cultivating animal cells in a safe and controlled environment.

[The Good Food Institute](https://gfi.org/science/the-science-of-cultivated-meat/) explains that the manufacturing process begins with acquiring and banking stem cells from an animal. These cells are then grown in bioreactors (known colloquially as [cultivators](https://gfi.org/cultivated/)) at high densities and volumes. The cells are fed an oxygen-rich cell culture medium containing basic nutrients such as amino acids, glucose, fats, vitamins, and inorganic salts, and typically supplemented with growth factors and other proteins.

As of [June 2026](https://gfi.org/resource/where-cultivated-meat-can-be-sold/), cultivated meat can be sold in Singapore, the United States, and Australia. A total of seven companies (UPSIDE Foods, GOOD Meat, Vow, Wildtype, Mission Barns, Believer Meats, and Gourmey/PARIMA) have received regulatory clearance in certain countries to sell multiple different cultivated meat products. The most recent instance was in [April 2026](https://parima.bio/blog/parima-becomes-the-first-european-company-to-obtain-culitvated-food-approval-across-two-species), when PARIMA secured regulatory approval for cultivated duck from the Singapore Food Agency (SFA). 

The complete list as of June 30, 2026 is as follows:

|  # | Jurisdiction | Agency             | Company        | Product Type   | Approval Status    | Year of First Approval |
| -: | ------------ | ------------------ | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------: |
|  1 | Singapore    | SFA                | GOOD Meat      | Chicken        | Complete           |                   2020 |
|  2 | USA          | FDA & USDA         | UPSIDE Foods   | Chicken        | Complete           |                   2023 |
|  3 | USA          | FDA & USDA         | GOOD Meat      | Chicken        | Complete           |                   2023 |
|  4 | Singapore    | SFA                | Vow            | Quail          | Complete           |                   2024 |
|  5 | Australia/NZ | FSANZ              | Vow            | Quail          | Complete           |                   2025 |
|  6 | USA          | FDA                | Wildtype       | Salmon         | Complete           |                   2025 |
|  7 | USA          | FDA & USDA         | Mission Barns  | Pork fat       | Complete           |                   2025 |
|  8 | USA          | FDA & USDA         | Believer Meats | Chicken        | Complete           |                   2025 |
|  9 | Singapore    | SFA                | PARIMA         | Chicken        | Complete           |                   2025 |
| 10 | Hong Kong    | FEHD               | Vow            | Quail          | Partially complete |                        |
| 11 | Israel       | Ministry of Health | Aleph Farms    | Beef           | Partially complete |                        |
| 12 | Singapore    | SFA                | PARIMA         | Duck fois gras | Complete           |                   2026 |
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve **Yes** if, after June 30, 2026 and before July 1, 2027, at least one new cultivated meat product receives regulatory approval for commerical sale in any country.

The cultivated meat product can be either a blended or standalone product, but must be approved by a national regulatory agency for human consumption and not be of the same "Product Type" as one with an existing regulatory approval in the same country. For example, if another product with type "Chicken" was approved in Singapore, this question wouldn't resolve, because GOOD Meat has already received approval in Singapore for cultivated chicken.

The [Good Food Institute's cultivated meat tracker](https://gfi.org/resource/where-cultivated-meat-can-be-sold/) will be used as the primary resolution source but another credible source may be used in case the tracker becomes unreliable or ceases to exist.

question: Will Instructure be subject to another major hack before September 1, 2026?
background:
Instructure is the company behind Canvas LMS, used by [41%](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Canvas_security_incident) of North American higher education institutions for coursework, exams, grading, and student communication. In the last eight months, it has been hacked twice by [ShinyHunters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ShinyHunters), a black-hat criminal hacking and extortion group.

In September 2025, ShinyHunters [accessed Instructure's Salesforce environment](https://www.instructure.com/resources/blog/security-incident-update), compromising business contact information. Then in late April 2026, the group [exploited a vulnerability in Canvas's Free-For-Teacher accounts](https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/05/12/congress-investigates-canvas-breach-after-instructure-cuts-deal-with-shinyhunters/5238927) to exfiltrate an estimated 3.65 terabytes of data — including names, emails, student IDs, and billions of private messages — affecting approximately 275 million users across 8,809 institutions. After Instructure attempted to patch the vulnerability without negotiating, the ShinyHunters [re-entered on May 7 through the same vulnerability](https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/05/12/congress-investigates-canvas-breach-after-instructure-cuts-deal-with-shinyhunters/5238927), defacing login pages with ransom demands and triggering a global Canvas outage during exams week, leading many universities to postpone finals. Instructure [ultimately paid a ransom](https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/11/instructure-pays-ransom-canvas-hackers) in exchange for data destruction and assurances against further extortion.

[At least three class-action lawsuits have been filed](https://www.abc4.com/news/wasatch-front/lawsuits-instructure-data-breach/) alleging Instructure failed to protect user data (including that of minors) and that the outage cut off access to materials students needed to study for finals. The [U.S. House Homeland Security Committee has summoned CEO Steve Daly](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/13/us-lawmakers-demand-answers-from-instructure-after-canvas-data-breaches/) for a briefing by May 21, 2026, and the [FBI, CISA, and Department of Education are all engaged](https://fsapartners.ed.gov/knowledge-center/library/electronic-announcements/2026-05-12/technology-security-alert-ongoing-cybersecurity-incident-involving-canvas-learning-management-system). Instructure [states that Canvas is fully operational with enhanced security measures](https://www.instructure.com/incident_update), though its forensic investigation remains ongoing.

Cybersecurity experts have [noted that paying the ransom risks incentivizing future attacks](https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/11/instructure-pays-ransom-canvas-hackers). The sheer concentration of educational infrastructure on a single platform means another breach would compound reputational, legal, and operational damage at a scale difficult to absorb.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, after the question's opening and before September 1, 2026, Instructure or any of its [products](https://www.instructure.com/products) (including but not limited to Canvas, Mastery, Parchment, and Impact) experiences at least one cybersecurity incident that meets any of the following conditions:

1. **Data exfiltration:** An unauthorized party obtains personal data (such as names, email addresses, student IDs, messages, credentials, or financial information) of at least 10,000 users.
2. **Service disruption:** One or more Instructure products are rendered substantially unavailable to at least 100 institutional customers for a continuous period of at least 4 hours as a direct result of a security breach.
3. **Ransom or extortion demand:** A threat actor issues a ransom or extortion demand related to data or systems access newly obtained from Instructure.

All conditions require confirmation from at least one of the following: Instructure official communications, credible news reporting, or government disclosures. An attacker's public claim alone will not be sufficient.

question: Will Iceland vote Yes in the 2026 EU negotiations referendum?
background:
According to tradition, in 874, [Ingólfr Arnarson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ing%C3%B3lfr_Arnarson) and his family became the first Icelanders when they set off from what is now Norway and settled in what would become Reykjavík. Over the next thousand years, Iceland would be independent, part of Norway, part of the [Kalmar Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalmar_Union), and part of Denmark, before becoming an independent republic in 1944 following [a referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_Icelandic_constitutional_referendum) in which over 99% of over 70,000 voters opted to dissolve ties with Denmark and adopt a new constitution.

However Iceland has in many ways retained political ties to the continent. In 1950, shortly after its formation, Iceland joined the Council of Europe. And although never part of the European Union (EU) or its predecessor, the European Economic Community, Iceland in 1970 joined the [European Free Trade Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Free_Trade_Association), in 1994 joined the [European Economic Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Area), and in 1996 joined the [Schengen Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area). Thus, for decades, Icelanders have participated in a common market and travel area with virtually all EU member states.

In 2008, after Iceland fell into a [severe financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%932011_Icelandic_financial_crisis), the prime minister resigned, and snap elections were called. In the run-up to [the election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Icelandic_parliamentary_election), the interim prime minister, Johanna Sigurðardóttir, stated that, if reelected, she would prioritize EU membership as a way of helping Iceland emerge from the crisis. In the end, her Social Democratic Alliance received the most votes, and she continued on as prime minister, and within months Iceland had applied to join the EU.

EU accession negotiations began in 2010, but public opinion began to sour on the idea, and, in 2013, after closing 11 out of 33 acquis chapters, Iceland [elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Icelandic_parliamentary_election) a Euroskeptic government, which suspended Iceland's accession process and dissolved the negotiating committee. Iceland's application to join the EU, though never formally withdrawn, has been frozen ever since.

After the [2024 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Icelandic_parliamentary_election), the Social Democratic Alliance regained the premiership, and the new government declared that Iceland would have another referendum, about whether to resume the EU application process. [That referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Icelandic_European_Union_membership_negotiations_referendum) is scheduled to take place on August 29, 2026.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if *Já.* (Yes.) receives the most votes in the 2026 [referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Icelandic_European_Union_membership_negotiations_referendum) on whether Iceland should resume accession negotiations with the European Union.

question: Will the Japan Self-Defense Forces have tested a Tomahawk missile by mid-2027?
background:
There is currently a growing security competition in Northeast Asia, with Japan seeking to boost its defense capabilities amid increasing threats from China and North Korea. 

The Tomahawk cruise missile is a long-range, all-weather, subsonic cruise missile that can be launched from a variety of platforms, including ships, submarines, and land-based systems. It is designed to attack a variety of targets, including ships, ground vehicles, and buildings. The missile has a range of over 1,000 miles, making it capable of hitting targets on mainland China from peripheral regions of Japan.

[Japan is considering purchasing hundreds of U.S.-built Tomahawk cruise missiles as part of a major defense buildup,](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2022/12/12/japan-tomahawk-missiles-ukraine-war/) marking a significant break with its long-standing tradition of avoiding offensive weapons. The move comes as China undergoes a military modernization and North Korea continues its nuclear program. Japan is also set to unveil its new national security and defense strategies this month, along with a major increase in defense spending. These moves may indicate, as well as contribute to, increased tensions in Northeast Asia and the broader Indo-Pacific region.

Article 9 of the Japanese Constitution renounces war as a means of settling international disputes and prohibits Japan from maintaining land, sea, and air forces. However, a 2014 reinterpretation of the constitution allowed for military action in the event an ally is attacked. The purchase of Tomahawk cruise missiles, which would previously have been considered offensive weapons, would mark a significant break with Japan's long-standing tradition of avoiding such weapons and could have significant political implications.
resolution_criteria:
Metaculus admins will resolve this question as **Yes** or **No** according to credible published sources and the self-reports of the Japan Self-Defense Forces, the Japan Defense Agency, and the Japanese government.

Tested means a full, integrated flight test in which a Tomahawk missile is launched, navigates towards a target, and hits it

question: Will the Lebanese Armed Forces deploy to the initial two pilot zones in southern Lebanon before September 2026?
background:
On June 26, 2026, the United States brokered a [trilateral framework agreement](https://www.state.gov/releases/office-of-the-spokesperson/2026/06/trilateral-framework-between-the-united-states-of-america-the-state-of-israel-and-the-republic-of-lebanon) between Israel and Lebanon in Washington following four days of talks. Under the agreement, Israel agreed to withdraw from two areas in southern Lebanon [(one north of the Litani River, one south)](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2026/06/30/israel-tells-lebanon-that-leaving-pilot-zones-will-take-time/), with the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) assuming control as a pilot initiative. Under the framework, Israel will remain in the broader southern Lebanon security zone until Hezbollah is disarmed.

Hezbollah was not party to the talks and has explicitly rejected the framework. The LAF deployment is the operational test of whether this framework holds: if LAF deploys successfully, it creates facts on the ground that reduce the need for Israel Defense Forces (IDF) presence. If it fails, the framework collapses and the ceasefire architecture is at risk.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if the Lebanese Armed Forces have physically deployed military units to the two initial pilot zones specified in the June 26, 2026 Washington trilateral framework agreement for a minimum of seven days before 12:01am ET on September 1, 2026, according to official statements from the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), the Lebanese Armed Forces or credible reporting from Reuters or the Associated Press.

question: Will the Federal Reserve raise the federal funds target range before July 30, 2026?
background:
CNBC May 2026: [The Fed will have to raise interest rates in July to appease ‘bond vigilantes,’ Yardeni says](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/18/the-fed-will-have-to-raise-interest-rates-in-july-to-appease-bond-vigilantes-yardeni-says.html)

>In statements prior to taking over the chair’s position, \[Fed Chair Kevin] [Warsh has said he believes](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/16/kevin-warsh-comes-into-the-fed-facing-a-big-family-fight-over-cutting-interest-rates.html) the Fed can lower its benchmark interest rate from its current targeted range of 3.5% to 3.75%. However, a [recent surge in inflation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/12/cpi-inflation-april-2026-.html), triggered largely by the Iran war but also owning to other underlying factors, has led to markets repricing rate expectations. But it’s gotten more complicated with Warsh’s arrival: Not only does the market not believe the Fed will cut, but odds also are rising for a hike, with current pricing implying a 42% chance of an increase by the end of the year, according to the CME Group’s [FedWatch](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html?redirect=/trading/interest-rates/countdown-to-fomc.html) tool. \[Market veteran Ed] Yardeni, though, thinks it will come sooner than that. While he sees the Fed holding steady at the June meeting, he believes a rate increase of a quarter percentage point is “likely” in July.
resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before July 30, 2026, the United States Federal Reserve announces an increase in the federal funds [target range](https://www.federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/fedexplained/accessible-version.htm) relative to 3.5%–3.75%.

question: Will Keir Starmer cease to be Prime Minister of the UK during 2026?
background:
[Keir Starmer]() is the Prime Minister of United Kingdom and leader of the Labour Party. Following the [2024 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_Kingdom_general_election), Starmer has faced immense backlash and unpopularity from across British politics, with mass public dissatisfaction on nearly every issue. As of December 2025, Starmer faces an immense -50 [approval rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leadership_approval_opinion_polling_for_the_next_United_Kingdom_general_election), with some polls reaching as low as -60.

Facing pressure from both the right wing Reform UK and the left wing Green Party, Labour's polling numbers have steadily declined from the already historically low 33.7% election victory, [to an average of 20%](https://electionmaps.uk/polling/vi), with some polls placing the party as low as 14%.

Due to Starmer's immense unpopularity, speculation has emerged of a leadership challenge, with contenders such as [Andy Burnham](https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cgq4zd0lx12t) and [Wes Streeting](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9v124znrgmo) emerging as contenders. Media has since repeatedly speculated on Starmer's prospects as leader, focusing on the possibility for him to be ousted following a potentially disastrous performance in the [2026 Local Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Kingdom_local_elections).
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, at any point before January 1, 2027, Keir Starmer ceases to be Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

question: Will Shakira's "Dai Dai" outpeak Shakira's "Waka Waka" on the Billboard Hot 100?
background:
The [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026) will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, with matches scheduled from June 11 to July 19, 2026. It will be the first World Cup to feature 48 teams and the first co-hosted by three nations.

On May 14, 2026, FIFA released ["Dai Dai"](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/shakira-burna-boy-dai-dai-official-song) by Shakira and Burna Boy as the Official FIFA World Cup 2026 Song, in support of the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund. The song was unveiled at the Maracana Stadium and released globally across streaming platforms.

The benchmark for this question is Shakira's ["Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waka_Waka_\(This_Time_for_Africa\)), the official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa. Waka Waka peaked at **#38 on the US** [Billboard Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/). It became the best-selling World Cup song of all time and one of the most-viewed music videos on YouTube, with multi-platinum certifications in numerous markets.

For comparison, here is how the official songs of the three most recent tournaments performed on the US Hot 100:

* **2014 Brazil** — ["We Are One (Ole Ola)"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_One_\(Ole_Ola\)) by Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez & Claudia Leitte peaked at **#11** on the Hot 100 (the only post-2010 World Cup song to outpeak Waka Waka).
* **2018 Russia** — ["Live It Up"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_It_Up_\(Nicky_Jam_song\)) by Nicky Jam, Will Smith & Era Istrefi did not chart on the Hot 100.
* **2022 Qatar** — ["Hayya Hayya (Better Together)"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayya_Hayya_\(Better_Together\)) and ["Tukoh Taka"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoh_Taka) neither charted on the Hot 100.
  Several factors may influence "Dai Dai"'s chart performance.

The tournament being co-hosted by the United States, the world's largest music market and the basis for the Billboard Hot 100, could increase the likelihood of a US chart hit. Shakira herself has an established US chart presence, and Burna Boy is one of the most globally successful Afrobeats artists, having previously charted on the Hot 100.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves **Yes** if "Dai Dai" by Shakira & Burna Boy achieves a peak position on the Billboard Hot 100 (US) of #37 or higher at any point on or before July 31, 2026.

The peak position will be determined according to the weekly [Billboard Hot 100 charts](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/).

question: Will Pope Leo XIV visit another country other than Spain before September 2026?
background:
Papal travel outside Rome has historically been rare. Since [Pope Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI "Pope Paul VI") (1963–1978), however, more pastoral trips have occurred. With advances in technology, mass media and global connectivity, as well as a shift in the Church's leadership, the [Pope's international travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_travel) has become more common. 

On May 8, 2025, the Papacy of [Pope Leo XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV) commenced after the passing of Pope Francis. Since then [the Pope has visited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_pastoral_trips_made_by_Pope_Leo_XIV) Turkey, Lebanon, Monaco, Algeria, Cameroon, Angola and Equatorial Guinea. His Holiness is also set to visit [Spain from June 6 to 12](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/events/event.dir.html/content/vaticanevents/en/2026/6/6/viaggio-spagna.html)[, 2026](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/events/event.dir.html/content/vaticanevents/en/2026/6/6/viaggio-spagna.html). Although apostolic journeys are often set well in advance, global conflicts, natural disasters and humanitarian crises can precipitate such events.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if Pope Leo XIV officially visits a country other than Spain or Italy after May 18, 2026 and before September 1, 2026, according to the official [Vatican calendar of events for the Pope](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/events/year.dir.html/2026.html). Merely passing through a country's airspace, landing at an airport or otherwise making a transitory visit will not count towards resolution.

If Pope Leo XIV ceases to be Pope before September 2026 this question will be **annulled**.

question: Will the USMCA be extended promptly at its July 2026 joint review?
background:
The [United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement](https://crsreports.congress.gov/product/pdf/IF/IF10997) (USMCA) is a trade deal between the United States, Mexico, and Canada that replaced the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). Signed on November 30, 2018, and implemented on July 1, 2020, the USMCA aimed to modernize trade relations and address issues that had emerged since NAFTA's implementation in 1994.

The USMCA [will undergo a review period](https://ustr.gov/sites/default/files/files/agreements/FTA/USMCA/Text/34_Final_Provisions.pdf) on its sixth anniversary, where it will be extended for another 16 years if all parties agree to extend it. If the parties do not agree to extend the USMCA, it will trigger an annual review process held each year until the deal expires in 2036 unless an extension is agreed to at one of the annual reviews. The Trump administration [pushed for the review process](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/usmca-review-upcoming-elections-and-a-path-forward/) and some observers expect that if Trump is president during the review he will push for significant changes. [Biden has also taken a protective stance on trade](https://www.thedialogue.org/analysis/will-the-usmca-accord-survive-an-upcoming-review/) and may push for changes more favorable to key US industries. It is possible that a contentious review process could lead to one or more parties withholding consent for an extension.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, following the joint review of the USMCA held in July 2026, the USMCA is extended for another 16-year period. The question will resolve as **No** if the joint review ends without extension, triggering the annual review process described in paragraph 4 of [Article 34.7 of the USMCA](https://ustr.gov/sites/default/files/files/agreements/FTA/USMCA/Text/34_Final_Provisions.pdf).

question: Will the market capitalization for USDT & USDC stablecoins surpass $300 billion USD by June 30, 2026?
background:
Stablecoins Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) have become linchpins of the cryptocurrency ecosystem, offering a bridge between volatile digital assets and traditional fiat currencies. As of early 2025, their combined market capitalization hovers around \$150–\$200 billion USD, according to data from CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap, with [<u>USDT</u>](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/tether/) dominating as the most widely used stablecoin globally and [<u>USDC</u>](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/usd-coin/) gaining traction among institutional players for its transparency and regulatory compliance. These assets underpin decentralized finance (DeFi), facilitate trading on crypto exchanges, and serve as a store of value in regions with unstable local currencies.

This forecast—whether USDT and USDC’s combined market cap will surpass \$300 billion by June 30, 2026—is significant because it tests the trajectory of stablecoin adoption amid shifting macroeconomic winds. Analysts suggest that renewed U.S. Federal Reserve easing, potentially driven by rising inflation or Treasury market pressures, could flood markets with liquidity, [<u>spurring demand for stablecoins as a hedge or transactional medium</u>](https://cryptohayes.medium.com/the-bbc-a33ddb3ce00b). Current Fed policies, with rates steady above 4% as of early 2025, face scrutiny as [<u>10-year Treasury yields climb toward 4.5%</u>](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10), hinting at conditions that might force monetary expansion. Conversely, regulatory risks loom large—[<u>USDT’s past opacity and potential U.S. clampdowns on stablecoin issuers could stall growth</u>](https://www.forbes.com/investing/worlds-largest-stablecoins/).

The implications are profound. A \$300 billion market cap would [<u>signal deeper integration of crypto into mainstream finance</u>](https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2025/03/stablecoins-digital-currencies-rise/), challenging banks and amplifying stablecoins’ role in cross-border payments and DeFi liquidity pools. It could also reflect a flight to digital safety nets if inflation exceeds 4% annually, [<u>as some predict</u>](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/). For traders, developers, and policymakers, this question probes whether stablecoins will solidify as the backbone of a new financial paradigm—or face a ceiling as global authorities and competing digital currencies, like CBDCs, close in.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve to YES if by June 30th, 2026, the total market cap for both USDT and USDC stablecoins - according to CoinGecko OR CoinMarketCap - is greater than \$300 billion USD.

question: Before July 1, 2026, will the U.S. Supreme Court agree to hear a case that could end the constitutional right to same-sex marriage?
background:
The US Supreme Court's 2015 decision in *Obergefell v. Hodges* [held](https://www.oyez.org/cases/2014/14-556) in a 5-4 opinion that the due process clause of the 14th Amendment guarantees the right to marriage to both opposite-sex couples and same-sex couples. In the 2022 *Dobbs* decision overturning *Roe v. Wade*, Justice Clarence Thomas [wrote](https://www.politico.com/news/2022/06/24/thomas-constitutional-rights-00042256) a concurring opinion saying that the Court "should reconsider" its decision in Obergefell. In response, Congress passed the bipartisan [Respect for Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respect_for_Marriage_Act) codifying many protections for same-sex marriage, which was signed by then-President Joe Biden on December 13, 2022.

On January 20, 2025, Donald J. Trump was inaugurated as the 47th President of the United States. In the months following, several states [introduced legislation](https://www.them.us/story/gay-marriage-rights-right-wing-overturn-kim-davis-state-legislatures) to roll back Obergefell, including four states offering "covenant marriages" between a man and woman. 

In July 2025, Kim Davis, a former Kentucky county clerk jailed in 2015 for refusing to issue a marriage license to  a gay couple on religious grounds, [filed an appeal](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/12/trump-same-sex-marriage/85614479007/) with the Supreme Court to have the Court overturn \$360,000 in emotional damages and attorneys' fees that a lower court held she must pay.

Obergefell's original 5-4 opinion was voted against by three current Supreme Court Justices: Clarence Thomas, Chief Justice John Roberts, and Samuel Alito. Justice Neil Gorsuch, who joined the Court after Obergefell, [wrote a dissertation](https://time.com/4705941/neil-gorsuch-gay-rights-same-sex-marriage/) mentioning it being "obvious" that the US Constitution does not support same-sex marriage. Other conservatives who have joined the Court since Obergefell, Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett, have refused to directly answer when asked about the decision. (See for example, [The Blade](https://www.washingtonblade.com/2018/09/12/kavanaughs-answers-leave-lgbt-legal-experts-unsatisfied/) and [The Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/video/politics/barrett-dodges-questions-on-obergefell-case-same-sex-marriage/2020/10/14/9e3e6a51-2489-4f20-8555-1f8c52d32351_video.html).)
resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2026, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) report that the U.S. Supreme Court has granted a petition for writ of certiorari in a case where a decision on the merits of a question presented could find that there is no constitutional right to marriage for same-sex couples and would thereby overturn the Supreme Court's decision in [Obergefell v. Hodges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obergefell_v._Hodges).

question: Will the U.S. Supreme Court further cut back campaign finance limitations in National Republican Senatorial Committee v. FEC before January 1, 2027?
background:
*This forecasting question is associated with the Verity controversy:* [*Will the U.S. Supreme Court reduce campaign finance limitations in National Republican Senatorial Committee v. Federal Election Commission?*](https://www.verity.news/controversy/Will-the-US-Supreme-Court-further-cut-back-campaign-finance-limitations-and-expand-on-the-Citizens-United-ruling-National-Republican-Senatorial-Committee-v-Federal-Election-Commission)

The Supreme Court’s 2010 decision in [*<u>Citizens United v. FEC</u>*](https://www.fec.gov/legal-resources/court-cases/citizens-united-v-fec/) fundamentally reshaped U.S. campaign finance law by holding that the First Amendment prohibits the government from restricting independent political expenditures by corporations and unions. This ruling overturned longstanding limits and led to the rise of [<u>super PACs</u>](https://www.opensecrets.org/political-action-committees-pacs/super-pacs/2022) — political committees that can raise and spend unlimited funds from individuals, corporations, and unions so long as they do not coordinate directly with candidates or parties. [<u>Advocates say the decision protected political speech, while critics argue it amplified wealthy interests in elections</u>](https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/research-reports/citizens-united-explained).

Since *Citizens United*, the Court has continued to interpret campaign finance restrictions through a robust free-speech lens. In later rulings such as [*<u>McCutcheon v. FEC</u>*<u> </u>](https://www.fec.gov/legal-resources/court-cases/mccutcheon-et-al-v-fec/)(2014), the Court struck down aggregate limits on individual contributions to federal candidates and committees, reasoning that such caps burden political speech without sufficiently preventing corruption. These decisions have cumulatively loosened regulatory controls and shifted much of the campaign finance landscape toward greater permissiveness.

The current case, [*<u>National Republican Senatorial Committee v. FEC</u>*](https://www.scotusblog.com/cases/case-files/national-republican-senatorial-committee-v-federal-election-commission/), represents the latest high-profile challenge. Plaintiffs including the NRSC, another Republican campaign committee, and individuals argue that federal limits on coordinated spending by political parties and their candidates violate the First Amendment in light of the Court’s recent free-speech jurisprudence. The [<u>U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear the case </u>](https://www.scotusblog.com/2025/12/court-to-hear-arguments-on-whether-to-further-cut-back-campaign-finance-limitations/)after the Sixth Circuit upheld the limits under older precedent. Oral arguments were heard in December 2025, and a [<u>decision is expected by mid-2026</u>](https://www.newsweek.com/supreme-court-let-political-parties-spend-unlimited-money-11164570).

A ruling for the plaintiffs could significantly expand *Citizens United*’s logic by striking down longstanding limits on party coordination and spending, potentially allowing parties to raise and spend far larger sums directly in conjunction with candidates. Conservative advocates have framed this as strengthening free speech rights, while critics warn it could [<u>further amplify wealthy donors’ influence and weaken anti-corruption safeguards</u>](https://www.whitehouse.senate.gov/news/release/whitehouse-highlights-amicus-brief-detailing-dark-money-corruption-after-oral-arguments-in-nrsc-v-fec/).

At the same time, legal observers note that the outcome is not certain; some justices expressed skepticism during oral argument about sweeping changes to campaign finance limits, and longstanding precedents like [*<u>FEC v. Colorado Republican Federal Campaign Committee</u>*](https://www.fec.gov/legal-resources/court-cases/fec-v-colorado-republican-federal-campaign-committee/) (2001) could still influence the Court’s reasoning.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if, before January 1, 2027, the U.S. Supreme Court issues a final merits decision in *National Republican Senatorial Committee v. Federal Election Commission* that strikes down, invalidates, or weakens federal limits on coordinated spending between political parties and their candidates, resulting in a clear expansion of permissible campaign-finance activity, such as allowing party committees to raise or spend more money in coordination with candidates than was allowed under prior law.

question: Will the U.S. Supreme Court rule in favor of Monsanto in Monsanto Company v. John L. Durnell?
background:
On April 4, 2025, Monsanto Company, a subsidiary of Bayer AG, filed a petition for a writ of certiorari with the U.S. Supreme Court in the case [Monsanto Company v. John L. Durnell](https://law.justia.com/cases/missouri/court-of-appeals/2025/ed112410.html). The case arises from a Missouri state court decision where a jury [awarded](https://blog.cvn.com/1.25m-verdict-in-zero-offer-case-breaks-monsantos-roundup-trial-winning-streak) \$1.25 million in damages to John L. Durnell, who alleged that exposure to Monsanto's glyphosate-based herbicide, Roundup, caused his non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.

Monsanto's [petition](https://content.presspage.com/uploads/2809/4203e574-9a0c-49ee-9476-8ba63ba6e424/4.4.2025monsantov.durnellcertpetition.pdf?10000) argued that the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) preempts state-law failure-to-warn claims, especially since the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has approved Roundup's labeling without a cancer warning. The petition highlighted a split among federal appellate courts on this preemption issue, noting that while the Third Circuit has held that FIFRA preempts such state-law claims, the Ninth and Eleventh Circuits have reached the opposite conclusion.

On January 16, 2026, the Supreme Court [agreed to hear the case](https://www.supremecourt.gov/docket/docketfiles/html/public/24-1068.html). The Court will decide whether federal pesticide law prevents plaintiffs from bringing state-law claims that Roundup should have included a cancer warning, given that EPA did not require such a warning.

Merits briefing has since been completed. The United States filed an [amicus brief supporting Monsanto](https://www.justice.gov/d9/2026-03/24-1068_monsanto_tsac.pdf), arguing that FIFRA preempts Durnell’s failure-to-warn claim, and the Court granted the Solicitor General’s request to participate in oral argument. The case was argued on April 27, 2026, with Paul Clement arguing for Monsanto, Sarah Harris for the United States, and Ashley Keller for Durnell. As of May 28, 2026, the Court has not issued a decision.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if the U.S. Supreme Court issues a decision that reverses, vacates, or otherwise sets aside the Missouri state court judgment against Monsanto, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

It will resolve as **No** if the Court issues a ruling affirming the judgment against Monsanto.

If the Court does not issue a decision before August 1, 2026, or dismisses the case without reversing, vacating, remanding, affirming, or otherwise disposing of the Missouri judgment, this question will be **annulled**.

question: Will the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) close above 30 on more than 5 trading days between April 20, 2026 and May 31, 2026?
background:
The [CBOE Volatility Index (VIX)](http://cboe.com/tradable_products/vix) is the most widely tracked measure of expected near-term volatility in U.S. equity markets, derived from implied volatility of S\&P 500 options contracts. Often called the "fear gauge," it rises sharply during periods of geopolitical stress, financial shock, or sudden risk repricing. In normal conditions the VIX trades between 12 and 20; crossing 30 is considered a meaningful institutional stress threshold: volatility-targeting funds, risk-parity strategies, and options overlays that collectively manage trillions in assets respond systematically to sustained VIX readings above this level. As of mid-April 2026, the VIX stands near 17.94, having reached a year-to-date high of 35.75 during the acute phase of the U.S.–Iran escalation in early April.

This question uses a threshold of more than 5 closing days above 30 — deliberately distinguishing a single-day spike (which may reflect a transient shock) from a sustained stress regime (which signals that markets are pricing in continued or renewed escalation rather than a return to diplomatic de-escalation). Conversely, a VIX that fails to cross 30 on more than 5 days through May 31 would suggest financial markets have absorbed the geopolitical shock and recalibrated toward a lower-risk baseline.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if the [official daily closing value](https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_historical_data?utm_source=chatgpt.com) of the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) is strictly greater than 30.00 on more than 5 trading days between April 20, 2026, and May 31, 2026, inclusive.

question: Will an AI model reach a 3 hour time horizon with 80% reliability during 2026?
background:
[METR](https://metr.org/) is an AI model evaluation and threat research organisation that studies AI capabilities and their ability to conduct AI research and self-improve.

METR regularly tests released models for their threat capacity, which includes measuring their ability to complete realistic software and research tasks reliably. For each task, they measure how long it takes humans with relevant expertise to complete it, then see which tasks different models can solve. By fitting a curve of model success against human task duration, they define each model's "[time horizons](https://metr.org/blog/2025-03-19-measuring-ai-ability-to-complete-long-tasks/)": the longest task length (in human time) on which the model can succeed with around 50% or 80% probability.

Their results show that these horizons have been growing exponentially over time. As of December 2025 the highest time horizon with an 80% chance of success is 31 minutes by [GPT-5.1-Codex-Max](https://evaluations.metr.org/gpt-5-1-codex-max-report/), a 5x improvement from 2024's best performer GPT-o1.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, during 2026, [METR estimates](https://metr.org/blog/2025-03-19-measuring-ai-ability-to-complete-long-tasks/) that an AI model has a time horizon of ≥3 hours at 80% reliability, i.e. the AI has an estimated ≥80% reliability on tasks requiring human experts ≥3 hours to solve.

question: Will Israel participate in the Eurovision Song Contest 2026?
background:
## **1. Eurovision Song Contest History and Israel Participation**

The Eurovision Song Contest, organized annually by the **European Broadcasting Union (EBU)** since 1956, brings together broadcasters from across Europe (and beyond) to compete with one song each. Israel has participated since 1973, winning four times, but its presence has often been controversial, drawing boycott campaigns and political debate.

Each year broadcasters must confirm their participation; the host country and the “Big Five” (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom) qualify directly for the Grand Final, while all other countries, including Israel, compete in the semi-finals.

## **2. Hamas Terrorist Attack and Gaza Genocide**

Israel’s response to 2023 attacks has been qualified as genocide by the IAGS (International Association of Genocide Scholars). [IAGS Resolution on the Situation in Gaz](https://genocidescholars.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/IAGS-Resolution-on-Gaza-FINAL.pdf)a.

The genocide has received strong public rejection in many of the countries participating in Eurovision. [YouGov study at EuroNews](https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/06/06/does-the-public-support-the-government-of-israel-in-western-european-countries)

Government positions have varied widely: some political parties and officials have called for BDS-aligned measures against Israel, while others have expressed support for Israel’s right to respond to Hamas or chosen to remain largely silent.

### **2.1 Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) Movement**

Activists, cultural figures, political parties, and NGOs have joined the BDS movement or similar initiatives to press for Israel's exclusion. Over 70 former Eurovision contestants signed an open letter in 2025 demanding that Israel (and its broadcaster Kan) be banned in connection with accusations over its actions in Gaza. [Letter and signatories](https://artistsforpalestine.org.uk/2025/05/06/former-eurovision-contestants-demand-exclusion-of-israel-from-contest/)

In several countries local campaigns pressured their country broadcaster to withdraw from Eurovision and/or to request EBU to exclude Israel.

## **3. Requests by Broadcasters / Countries to Discuss Israel Exclusion**

In 2024, several countries publicly called for Israel’s exclusion or threatened withdrawal, citing humanitarian concerns. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_2024#Calls_for_exclusion). In 2025, again several countries called for exclusion of Israel. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_2025#Calls_for_exclusion)

After Eurovision 2025, several broadcasters including RTVE, VRT, RTÉ, and others requested audits and reforms of the televoting system, citing transparency concerns after unusually high points for Israel, while some also questioned Israel’s future participation. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_2025#After_Eurovision)

## **4. EBU Assembly Discussing Israel Participation**

At the EBU Assembly, several member broadcasters called for a “serious and in-depth debate” on whether Israel should be allowed to participate in the Eurovision Song Contest 2026.The EBU acknowledged these concerns and said members had raised “deeply held views” but declined to vote in July, instead committing to further consultation among members.

The EBU has extended the deadline during which members (broadcasters) can withdraw without penalty until mid-December 2025, to allow time for decisions in light of this controversy.

(Refer to: [EBU Statement on Eurovision Song Contest General Assembly Discussion](https://www.ebu.ch/news/2025/07/ebu-statement-on-eurovision-song-contest-general-assembly-discussion))

## **5. Announcements of Conditional Withdrawal by Several Countries**

Some broadcasters have said they will *not participate* in Eurovision 2026 **if** Israel is allowed in. This is not just discussion: it’s a conditional withdrawal. Very clear statements have been officially communicated during September 2025:

* RTÉ (**Ireland**): “*Ireland will not take part in the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest, if the participation of Israel goes ahead*” [RTE](https://www.rte.ie/entertainment/2025/0911/1532957-rte-eurovision/) 12<sup>th</sup> September
* RTV SLO (**Slovenia)**: “*If Israel participates in the Eurovision Song Contest, we will not take part in it, is the clear position of RTV Slovenia.”*  [RTV SLO](https://www.rtvslo.si/zabava-in-slog/glasba/ema/ce-bo-izrael-nastopil-na-evroviziji-slovenije-ne-bo/757441) 12<sup>th</sup> September
* AVROTROS (**Netherlands**): “*AVROTROS' participation in the Eurovision Song Contest 2026 is not possible as long as Israel is admitted by the EBU*” [AVROTROS](https://www.avrotros.nl/article/avrotros-trekt-grens-bij-songfestival-2026~1176/)
* RTVE (**Spain**): “*Spain will withdraw from Eurovision if Israel continues in the contest.*” [RTVE](https://www.rtve.es/contenidos/documentos/decision_RTVE_eurovision.pdf) 16<sup>th</sup> September

Other broadcasters (e.g. in **Iceland** and **Belgium**) have expressed strong concerns or conditional positions but, as of 16<sup>th</sup> September 2025, the four countries above are the ones with official withdrawal announcements tied explicitly to Israel’s participation.

## **6. Israel’s Announced Intention to Participate**

The Israeli public broadcaster **Kan** has confirmed its intention to participate in Eurovision 2026.

Kan’s CEO, Golan Yochpaz, has defended Israel's participation amid the boycott threats, arguing that Eurovision must remain non-political, and that Israel should not be excluded. [Jerusalem Post](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/culture/article-867564?utm_source=chatgpt.com) September 15th 2025

## **7. EBU General Assembly**

The issue is expected to be revisited formally at the next General Assembly in **December 2025**, when a decision or resolution around Israel’s participation may be made.

Some media reports have suggested the EBU might propose that Israel compete under a *neutral flag*, or withdraw temporarily, but Israel and the EBU have denied formal offers of those alternatives. [Eurovoix news](https://eurovoix.com/2025/09/15/eurovision-2026-ebu-denies-reports-about-israel-competing-under-a-neutral-flag/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## **8. EBU and Eurovision Song Contest (ESC) rules**

The ESC is a non-political event (see the ESC rules [here](https://eurovision.tv/about/rules)), however, in 2022 Russian broadcasters were [suspended](https://www.ebu.ch/news/2022/02/ebu-statement-on-russia-in-the-eurovision-song-contest-2022) following the invasion of Ukraine. This was the only expulsion.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolves as **Yes** if Israel is officially listed among the participants in the Eurovision Song Contest 2026 by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) **and** Israel performs in one of the two semi-finals. The question will resolve as **No** if:

* Israel is not listed by the EBU, withdraws before the contest, or is disqualified such that it does not perform in a semi-final.
* Israel artists compete under a neutral flag.

question: Will shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz return to normal before April 27, 2026?
background:
The [Strait of Hormuz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz) is a narrow waterway that connects the Persian Gulf to the ocean, via the Gulf of Oman. The strait is bordered by Iran to the north and Oman and the United Arab Emirates to the south. Due to the amount of oil production in the Persian Gulf, 25% of the world's seaborne oil trade, as well as 20% of the world's liquefied natural gas, and a daily average of [60 ships](https://hormuzstraitmonitor.com/) has historically travelled through the strait. 

On February 28, 2026, Israel and the United States began [a sustained campaign of airstrikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war) against Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and attempting to topple the Iranian government. The strikes began a regional war, with Iran retaliating against Israel and the United States, as well as their assets in countries throughout the region. Shortly after the war began, Iran declared that ships would not be allowed to transit the strait, and on March 1, 2026, Iran [attacked several oil tankers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis).

A few days later, Iran clarified that the strait would be closed only to the U.S., Israel, and their western allies, and indeed Chinese, Turkish, and Saudi tankers have since been allowed to pass. However, the amount of [ship traffic](https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730) through the strait remains extremely low, and hundreds of ships remain [stranded](https://hormuzstraitmonitor.com/) in the Persian Gulf. As a result, global [oil prices](https://oilprice.com/oil-price-charts/) have skyrocketed.

U.S. President Donald Trump has made [conflicting statements](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/14/us-kharg-island-oil-export-hub) regarding how long the U.S. would continue to wage war, while the U.S has accused Iran of placing mines in the strait. Trump has [called on other nations](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/15/gulf-arab-states-intercept-new-missiles-and-drones-as-iran-threatens-to-widen-war-00829221) to send warships to the region in order to help reopen the strait but has [received muted reactions](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/15/world/middleeast/trump-strait-of-hormuz-iran-warships.html).
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if, after March 16, 2026 and before April 27, 2026, 45 or more ships transit through the Strait of Hormuz during a single day, as reported by [IMF Portwatch](https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730).

question: Will Anthropic be a designated supply chain risk on May 1, 2026?
background:
Under [10 U.S.C. § 3252](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/10/3252), the U.S. Secretary of Defense, of the Army, of the Navy, or of the Air Force may exclude certain "sources" from competing for government contracts (or subcontracts) for so-called [national security systems](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/44/3552#b_6) in order to reduce "supply chain risk." Supply chain risk is defined in the statute to mean the risk that an adversary may sabotage or subvert the relevant national security system.

Separately, under [41 U.S.C § 4713](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/41/4713), the head of an executive agency may exclude a "source" from competing for government contacts for certain information technology or telecommunications systems, in order to reduce supply chain risk. Similarly here, supply chain risk is defined to mean the risk that a person may sabotage or manipulate the system(s) in question. By law, a party excluded under this statute [may petition for judicial review](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/41/1327). In September 2025, [Acronis AG, a Swedish cybersecurity and data protection company](https://natlawreview.com/article/order-first-fascsa-order-has-been-issued-odni), became the first entity known to be excluded under this law.

question: Will any political party or coalition acquire a supermajority in the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary elections?
background:
In 2010, Viktor Orbán’s party, Fidesz–Hungarian Civic Alliance, together with [its ally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidesz%E2%80%93KDNP) the Christian Democratic People’s Party (KDNP), [won 52.7% of the vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Hungarian_parliamentary_election) but—because of the electoral system—secured 263 of 386 seats, a ⅔ supermajority, giving the party the ability to amend the constitution without the support of other parties.

And indeed the government then amended the constitution, enacting [the Fundamental Law of 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Hungary#2011_Constitution), under which: (i) Parliament shrank from 386 to 199 seats; (ii) Single-round voting replaced the old two-round system; (iii) a “Winner compensation” system was introduced; and (iv) Redistricting occurred. With these changes, a party with \~45–50% of the popular vote can acquire a two-thirds constitutional supermajority. Under the old rules, such a feat was much less likely.

Hungary's [electoral system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_system_of_Hungary#National_Assembly_elections) is neither purely majoritarian (e.g., winner-take-all, district-based elections), nor purely proportional (e.g., a party-list election where districts don't matter). Instead, it is a mixed system that favours the majoritarian approach. Of the 199 seats, 106 are District Seats (elected via first-past-the-post voting) and 93 are List Seats (elected based on total national proportion). But Hungary's system [differs from other Mixed Systems such as Germany's](https://archive.nytimes.com/krugman.blogs.nytimes.com/2014/02/28/hungary-an-election-in-question-part-3/) due to the "winner compensation" system under which the surplus votes for the winner in a district are added into the national votes, allowing the party that won the district to win extra List Seats as well. With the current electoral system in Germany the list tier is used to *correct* toward proportionality. In Hungary, the surplus mechanism can *magnify* the dominance of the district winner.

The [next Hungarian parliamentary elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Hungarian_parliamentary_election) are scheduled for April 12, 2026.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if any party or coalition acquires a ⅔ supermajority (i.e., at least 133 seats) in the first Hungarian parliamentary elections held after this question opens, according to official election results.

question: Will Keiko Fujimori advance to the runoff in the 2026 Peruvian presidential election?
background:
The first round of the [2026 Peruvian presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Peruvian_general_election) is scheduled to take place on April 12, 2026, in which the two candidates who receive the most votes will advance to a runoff.

Peru has long faced political crisis and unrest, including a decade-long military dictatorship during the 1970s. In 1992, following his victory in the 1990 presidential election, Alberto Fujimori [conducted a self-coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Peruvian_self-coup) with the backing of the military. His subsequent rule was characterised by [dictatorial control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plan_Verde) and [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_sterilization_in_Peru).

In 2000, Alberto Fujimori fled the country and resigned, resulting in a return to a competitive electoral system. Despite his exile and eventual arrest, a significant [Fujimorist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujimorism) force has remained in the country led by his daughter [Keiko Fujimori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiko_Fujimori). 

In the [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Peruvian_general_election), [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Peruvian_general_election), and [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Peruvian_general_election) elections, Keiko Fujimori advanced to 2nd round, losing extremely narrowly each time. In 2016 her party, Popular Force, achieved a majority in Congress, [beginning a period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_political_crisis_\(2016%E2%80%93present\)) characterised by extreme conflict between the Presidency and Congress.

In 2018, President Pedro Pablo Kuczynski resigned following a series of scandals and attempted impeachments. The following year, his former Vice President Martín Vizcarra [dissolved Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%932020_Peruvian_constitutional_crisis) resulting in a snap election. However, in 2020, he was [impeached and removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_impeachment_of_Mart%C3%ADn_Vizcarra), with Congress selecting [Francisco Sagast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Sagasti)i once [Manuel Merino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Merino) resigned after just 5 days in office.

In 2022, following his victory in the 2021 presidential election, Pedro Castillo [attempted to dissolve Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Peruvian_self-coup_attempt). Unlike his predecessor he was unsuccessful and was subsequently arrested. His Vice President, [Dina Boluarte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dina_Boluarte), then became one of the most unpopular leaders in the world, while allowing Congress to consolidate power. In October 2025, Dina Boluarte was [impeached and removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_of_Dina_Boluarte), with [José Jerí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Jer%C3%AD), President of Congress, becoming President. However on February 17, 2026, he too was removed, being replaced by [José María Balcázar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Balc%C3%A1zar).
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if Keiko Fujimori advances to the runoff in the [2026 Peruvian presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Peruvian_general_election).

question: Will a 1kt meteor strike take place during March or April 2026?
background:
A [meteoroid](https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/meteors-meteorites/) is a small object in outer space, typically made out of rock and iron. When a meteoroid enters Earth's atmosphere, it becomes known as a meteor. Though they range in size from microscopic to multi-kilometre asteroids, smaller sizes are more prevalent, with larger objects being exponentially less common.

Space agencies and organisations have long attempted to track meteors entering Earth's atmosphere, with the NASA [Fireball and Bolide database ](https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/)combining information from across the world.

Since the 1990s, attempts to comprehensively [track space objects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_near-Earth_object_observation_projects) have dramatically increased, with specific attention focused on [near-Earth objects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near-Earth_object). Although these efforts are thought to have identified the vast majority of civilisation-threatening objects, smaller objects have been too numerous and small to properly track.

The total impact energy of a meteor is determined both by its speed relative to Earth and its size. As such, higher energy events occur far less often.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if, after March 10, 2026, and before May 1, 2026, a natural meteor explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy of ≥1 kt.

question: Will the US and Iran agree to a ceasefire before May 2026?

question: What will be the outcome of Duane "Keffe D" Davis's Tupac Shakur murder trial by September 11, 2026?

It resolves to the option describing the jury's verdict if one has been returned: Guilty of first-degree murder if the jury convicts Davis of first-degree murder (regardless of the enhancement findings); Guilty of a lesser homicide offense if the jury acquits on first-degree murder but convicts on a lesser included homicide offense; Not guilty (full acquittal) if the jury acquits Davis on all homicide charges submitted to it.
